title: fix(runtime): a grant that holds no federation capability is no longer listed list_remote_tables / import_object
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9CM6p5wbc64wQfnaBYYFChi)_
Fixes #28938

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：MCP 的联邦工具 `list_remote_tables` / `import_object` 现在只列给真能调用它们的连接：请求持有 `manage_platform_settings` 或 `manage_metadata` 才列出，否则 `tools/list` 不再出现这两件。
- **为什么改**：只授权 `metadata:write` 的 OAuth 连接拿不到用户的系统能力（只有 `actions:execute` 才委托），所以以前列出这两件工具却每次调用都 403，管理员也一样。
- **风险与回滚**：没有任何原本能成功的调用变失败；只是"必然 403"变成"工具不在列表里"。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**：`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` 的 federation 段（`heldFederationCapabilities` 与按它决定是否挂上两件工具）；`mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts` 新增的四个用例。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts`，预期 8 个用例全绿。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。另有一个产品问题留给你：是否让只带 `metadata:write` 的连接也能用这两件工具（见报告 open_questions）。

## What changes

- `buildMcpBridge` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`) carries `listRemoteTables` / `importObject` only when the request's envelope holds `manage_platform_settings` (`FEDERATION_READ_CAPABILITY`) or `manage_metadata` (`FEDERATION_WRITE_CAPABILITY`). `wireBridgeTools` in `@objectstack/mcp` registers the pair only on a bridge carrying both members, so without them `tools/list` omits the pair. This is the shape `list_actions` already has: it hides an action its caller may not run.
- A new helper, `heldFederationCapabilities(ec)`, is the one read behind both the listing decision and the per-call gate in `federationService`. The listing and the call therefore cannot disagree.
- No change to `packages/mcp`, `packages/core` or `packages/spec`. The scope-to-set map (`scopesToAgentPermissionSets`) and the door's delegation rule (the user's system capabilities reach an agent only under `actions:execute`) are untouched.

## Why

The `/mcp` door gives an OAuth agent the delegating user's system capabilities only when the grant names `actions:execute` (`packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts`, `systemPermissions`). It does not do this through a permission set: `metadata:write` and `actions:execute` both map to `mcp_agent_restricted`. So a `metadata:write`-only grant holds `systemPermissions: []`, and both federation calls always answered `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`. That held even for an administrator who holds both capabilities, yet the grant was listed both tools.

The card's other route was to judge the human's own capability under `metadata:write`. That route was measured and not taken, because it would let a grant do more than the published consent text says. The consent text for `metadata:write` (`MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_CONSENT_COPY`, `packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts`) is: "Build and change this app's metadata as drafts, within your own permissions — a person publishes them". `import_object` saves a live object at once, not a draft, and `list_remote_tables` reads a live remote schema. Neither is what that sentence promises. Whether `metadata:write` alone should carry them is the maintainer's call, and it is raised in the report.

## Tests

`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts` gains four cases. Each envelope is resolved by the real `/mcp` door (`resolveExecutionContext` with an OAuth token), not written by hand. The delegating user's set carries both federation capabilities unless stated otherwise:

1. `metadata:write` only, administrator: the envelope measures `systemPermissions: []`, the bridge carries neither member, and the service is never looked up.
2. `metadata:write` + `actions:execute`, same administrator: both members are present, and both calls reach the service.
3. `metadata:write` + `actions:execute`, user holding only `manage_metadata`: the pair is kept, and `list_remote_tables` still refuses `code: PERMISSION_DENIED`, `status: 403`.
4. `metadata:write` + `actions:execute`, user holding neither capability: neither member.

No existing test was edited.

## Acceptance notes

- For a grant that holds no federation capability, a `tools/call` on either tool now gets the SDK's unknown-tool answer instead of the 403 envelope. This is the same answer `create_record` gets without `data:write`. No call that succeeded before fails now.
- API keys and sessions are still not served the pair. That gate is `grantsAuthoringTools` in `@objectstack/mcp`, which is unchanged, and its pin was ablation-verified below.
- The MCP dogfood suite has no federation case, so none was added.

## Verification

Head: `2a88bf5b9` (merge of `origin/main` at `dedc35051`).

<details><summary>Red first on the main code (test commit bf746d06, fix not applied)</summary>

```
× a metadata:write-only grant for an administrator carries neither member: no call of it could pass
× a delegating user holding neither capability is carried neither member
AssertionError: expected 'function' to be 'undefined' // Object.is equality
Tests  2 failed | 6 passed (8)
```

A one-off probe on the same main code, deleted afterwards, measured the card's symptom: a `metadata:write`-only administrator gets `list PERMISSION_DENIED 403 | import PERMISSION_DENIED 403`.
</details>

<details><summary>Green and package suites</summary>

- `vitest run src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts`: 8/8 passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` (pre-merge head 7de225bd + changeset): Test Files 514 passed (514), Tests 8322 passed | 19 skipped. VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two touched source files: exit 0.
- After merging `origin/main` and rebuilding the runtime closure: `vitest run src/domains/mcp-federation-bridge.test.ts src/security/resolve-execution-context.test.ts` 48/48 passed; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` VERDICT command-exit 0.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs; mutation landed and was restored to the HEAD blob each time)</summary>

1. Always carry the pair (`...(heldFederationCapabilities(ec).length > 0` → `...(true`): cases 1 and 4 fail, `expected 'function' to be 'undefined'`. 2 failed | 6 passed.
2. Drop the per-call gate (`if (!heldFederationCapabilities(ec).includes(required)) {` → `if (false) {`): case 3 and the existing "refuses 403 without the capability" pin fail. 2 failed | 6 passed.
3. Serve keys and sessions (`grantsAuthoringTools`: `Array.isArray(grantedScopes) &&` → `!Array.isArray(grantedScopes) ||`, in `packages/mcp`): "registers neither for a key or a session…" and the skill-parity pin fail. 2 failed | 7 passed.
</details>

<details><summary>Derived gates (dispatch-gates --commands, 60 families, on head 2a88bf5b9)</summary>

On the merged head all 60 exited 0. `--ran` reconciliation, with every exit code recorded: 60 derived, 60 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

On the pre-merge head, two families had first exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET). `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` lacked `dist/` for packages outside the runtime closure. `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` was missing its pinned fixture commit in the shallow clone, and `git fetch` of that commit fixed it. Both are green in the run above.
</details>
